2. This writ petition is filed by the father of detenu-Paramkusam Roshan challenging the order of detention made under Section 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land- Grabbers,

sentences.text: 3. Heard Ms.Godugula Vijaya Lakshmi, learned counsel appearing for Sri S.Chalapathi Rao, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for home.

4. The detaining authority resorted to extraordinary measure of preventively detaining the detenu on the ground of involvement in four crimes and also considered the history of involvement of the detenue in two other crimes and securing bails in all the crimes.
According to the detaining authority the detenu is in the habit of committing crimes, securing bail and after securing bail indulging in committing crimes.

5. According to learned counsel for the petitioner, the crimes reported against the detenu are all routine law and order crimes and do not attract disturbance to public order warranting initiation of proceedings under the Act 1 of 1986 and preventively detaining the detenu.

She would submit that the detenu was wrongly implicated in the crimes and on due consideration of the application to grant bail, bail was granted in all the cases and without taking steps to seek cancellation of bail, if what is alleged by the prosecution is true, the detaining authority could not have resorted to the extreme measure of preventively detaining the detenu affecting his right to life and liberty.

6. According to learned Government Pleader, as can be seen from the narration of events noticed in the order of detention, the detenu is in the habit of involving in crimes and sofar, six crimes are registered against him.
He would submit that detenue committed heinous crime of murdering a driver for gain, stealing the vehicle and mobile phone.
The crime was committed in a gruesome manner and if detenu is allowed to go scot-free, he may indulge in committing similar crimes, which will disturb the public order.
7. From the narration of what transpired leading to death of the driver in Cr.No.19 of 2021, it appears that an altercation took place between the detenu and the victim.
In the process the victim collapsed, became unconscious, and then he was pushed into a small canal.

The detenue threw Yougender Swamy vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others on 16 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116545069/
2 stones and clay pellets on the deceased resulting in his instantaneous death.

sentences.text: Further, it appears that the car was not recovered from his possession.
This instance though indicate criminal bent of mind but by such solitary action it cannot be assumed that he would be indulging in committing such crimes in future.
8. The two crimes referred to in the order were noted for the purpose of considering the criminal background.
They were committed in years 2018 and 2019.

Of the four crimes relied upon to pass the order of detention, though Cr.No.22 of 2021 was registered on 01.02.2021 the incident against which the said crime was registered alleged to have taken place on 24.08.2019.

Thus, leaving the two crimes referred to assess criminal background and one crime referred to in the order of detention as not proximate to take decision to order preventive detention only three crimes are relevant for consideration by the detaining authority.
9. We are of the opinion that having regard to the nature of crimes reported against the detenu, it cannot be said that the involvement in those crimes would disturb the public order.
They are normal law and order crimes.
Ordinary law of the land is sufficient to deal with the situation.
It cannot be said that crimes registered against detenu inevitably lead to harm, danger or alarm or feeling of insecurity among the general public.

10. We hasten to make it clear that the observations made herein are only for the purpose of considering validity of the detention order and cannot come in the way of conducting trial as and when charge sheets are filed.

11. The Writ Petition is allowed and the respondents are directed to set the detenu namely Paramkusham Roshan S/o.Yugender Swamy, Aged about 20 yrs, Caste: Shathani Vyshnava, Occu :
Cable Operator R/o.H.No.3-124, Gudiwada Chowrastha, Palakurthy (V& M) of Jangaon District at liberty forthwith if he is no longer required in any other criminal case. Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
__________________ P.NAVEEN RAO,J ______________________ Dr. G.RADHA RANI,J 16th February, 2022 Rds Yougender Swamy vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others on 16 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116545069/
